title: "Priority placement" with a guaranteed shortlist paid to a personal UPI vs. job portal openly selling a paid visibility service
summary: A caller from NaukriHub phones a registered job seeker about improving their chances for roles such as a Vistara Infotech opening. In the fraud case, the caller sells "priority placement" that guarantees a shortlist or offer, payable to a personal UPI ID, with a refund promise. In the legitimate case, a NaukriHub sales executive openly sells a paid profile-highlight subscription, says plainly that it only increases visibility and guarantees no interview or job, that applying is free without it, and that payment happens only through the portal's own checkout with a GST invoice. **The legitimate label rests on transparent disclosure and the official payment channel, not on the absence of payment.**

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a job seeker with an active NaukriHub profile, seeking an operations or sales role at [AMOUNT_1] (₹25,000–₹45,000 per month); details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both calls mention the recipient's profile views, recruiter interest, a paid plan, and a price.
Both callers are selling something; money is requested in both.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller takes payment to a personal account for an outcome no portal can sell (a guaranteed shortlist or offer from a named employer).
stable_facts: Price: [AMOUNT_2] (₹3,000–₹12,000), called "priority placement" or "premium recruiter desk".
Paid to [UPI_ID_1], a personal handle; "the portal checkout does not have this plan".
Caller guarantees an interview and "near-certain" offer from Vistara Infotech, with full refund if not placed within 30 days.

legitimate.label_rationale: An openly paid, optional service is described accurately (what it does and does not do), and payment goes through the portal's own checkout with an invoice.
stable_facts: Plan: "Profile Highlight", [AMOUNT_3] (₹800–₹3,500) for three months, shown on the NaukriHub pricing page.
What it does: profile appears higher in recruiter searches and gets a badge.
What it does not do: no guaranteed interview, shortlist, or job; employers decide independently.
Payment only through the NaukriHub app or https://naukrihub.invalid/pricing, GST invoice issued; cancellable per stated terms. Applying to jobs stays free.

fraud: caller offers a "discount" and recipient declines
caller insists on the guarantee and recipient ends the call

caller tells a suspicious recipient to check the pricing page directly and not pay anyone by phone.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the price, strengthen the guarantee, or add urgency. They must not switch to OTPs, bank logins, or remote access. The legitimate caller may answer questions and accept a refusal; they must not claim any guarantee, push payment off-platform, or introduce any other charge after the branch.

must_preserve: profile-views framing and named employer identical across cases
_F guaranteed outcome with payment to [UPI_ID_1] at turn 7
_L "no guarantee", optional, in-app checkout with invoice
must_not_emit: real job portal names or real plan names

ambiguities: Payment is requested in both cases. _L is legitimate because the service is described accurately, is optional, and is paid through the platform's own channel with an invoice. A sales call being persistent is not evidence.
A "refund guarantee" does not make _F legitimate.

Distinct from jr_01: there, an agency charges a registration fee for a guaranteed job; here the caller impersonates the portal and sells a guaranteed outcome, and the counterpart is a real paid product.

evidence_references.claim: A major IT employer warns that fraudulent agencies charge fees to promise interviews, and that fake offers appear on genuine job portals (CJ03)
Upfront payment and unrealistic promises are red flags in fake job schemes (C11)
